subject: Clarify telemetry storage & default TTL for request/response data
messages:
From: Lina Alvarez <lina@acme-corp.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on default telemetry retention for prompts/outputs

Hi Michael,

Hope you’re well — we’re doing a quick security review ahead of a pilot and I need a few clarifications about how Redwood stores request/response data by default. Specifically: 

- What is the default time-to-live (TTL) for raw request/response content (prompts + model outputs) for hosted API customers?
- Are prompts/outputs treated differently from structured logs/trace data?
- Where is that data stored by default (region/residency) and can we pin it to our region?
- Are there built-in deletion APIs or does deletion require a support ticket/contract change?

I attached a short SOC2 evidence template showing the fields our security team wants filled out (SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx). Can you point us to documentation or give us the short answers for the pilot?

Thanks,
Lina Alvarez
Security Operations
Acme Corp

--
Attachment: SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45 KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Alvarez <lina@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default telemetry retention for prompts/outputs

Hi Lina — thanks for the checklist and great questions. Short answers up front, then details: 

- Default TTL (hosted API): 30 days for prompt and model-output content in the telemetry/diagnostic store.
- Treatment: Prompts/outputs are stored as part of the request/response telemetry and are separate from aggregated operational logs (metrics/traces) which follow a different retention policy (90 days by default).
- Residency: Default storage follows the region you select when provisioning (us/eu/apac). For self-serve hosted customers the storage is colocated with the serving region; for Dedicated/Private you can pick on-prem/VPC options.
- Deletion: We provide a Delete Data API for on-demand deletion of stored request/response records (details below). Some data (billing records, abuse investigations, and items subject to legal hold) are retained as required.

We’ve attached a two-page summary (redwood-default-retention-summary.pdf) and I’m looping in Marissa and Neha for anything I miss on audit artifacts / residency proofs. If you want, we can run through the SOC2 template in a quick 30-min call.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

1) Can the 30-day TTL be shortened at the account level (e.g., set to 7 days) from the Console or API?
2) Does the Delete Data API remove records from backups/snapshots and any upstream analytics stores?
3) For data residency: if we choose EU region, is any portion of prompt/output content replicated to US-based analytics or support tools by default?

We prefer short bullet answers and any links to the exact API endpoints. Also, if there’s a Data Processing Agreement clause we should reference for residency language, please point us to it.

Lina

Hi Lina — answering the follow-ups with explicit links and short bullets: 

1) Account-level TTL override: 
- Hosted API: You can request a shorter retention via Console -> Settings -> Data Retention; self-serve options allow 7/14/30 day presets for most accounts. Very large enterprise/Dedicated customers can request custom TTLs (including "no storage") via a signed addendum.
- API: No direct TTL parameter on per-request basis (to avoid accidental data loss) — account-level setting is available and we surface it in the Management API (PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id}/retention). Link: https://console.redwood.ai/settings/data-retention

2) Delete Data API and backups: 
- Endpoint: POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/data:delete (see retention doc above).
- Behavior: Deletes matched request/response records from the primary telemetry store within the retention SLA (usually completes within 24–72 hours). Backups/snapshots are overwritten on their normal rotation; for hosted customers backups are retained for disaster recovery windows (up to 90 days) but deleted-record markers prevent restored snapshots from reintroducing deleted content to the active store.
- Exceptions: Records flagged for active investigations, abuse handling, or legal hold are not removable via the API until cleared by our legal/compliance team.

3) Residency and replication: 
- If you pick EU region, prompt/output content is stored in EU regions only for standard hosting. We do not replicate prompt/output payloads to US analytics or support tools by default.
- Operational metrics (aggregates, anonymized telemetry) may be used in SRE dashboards; those are aggregated and cannot be traced back to customer content.
- For certain support workflows customers can opt-in to share a session transcript with Redwood support (explicit consent / ticket-based).

4) Data Processing Agreement / Clauses: 
- Residency language and processing details are in section 4 (Data Storage and Processing) of our DPA: https://contracts.redwood.ai/dpa-2026.pdf. 

Next steps: Marissa will follow up with the exact SOC2 artifact mappings and Neha will provide the deletion API request example (curl + JSON). If this looks good, we can schedule the 30-min walkthrough.

Thanks — Michael
